slides.text: THIS DIAMOND IS SAID TO CURSE ITS OWNERS
The Hope Diamond. 45.52 carats. Deep blue. Worth an estimated quarter billion dollars or more.
Legend says it was stolen from the eye of a statue in India. That part was probably invented... but the story stuck.
It belonged to French royalty. Louis XVI and Marie Antoinette both lost their heads to the guillotine.
In 1792, during the French Revolution, the crown jewels were stolen. The diamond vanished.
It resurfaced in London, recut, and ended up with the Hope family. They went broke and had to sell it.
Its next famous owner, Evalyn Walsh McLean, lost her son in an accident, her daughter to an overdose, and her husband to a mental hospital.
She wore it almost everywhere. Legend says she even hung it on her dog's collar.
In 1958, jeweler Harry Winston gave it to the Smithsonian. He sent it by registered mail, in a plain brown package.
The mailman who delivered it? Legend says he had a run of bad luck right after. It's still on display in Washington, D.C.
